clue.text: Degree of spirit regarding publicity shown in check for errors

parts.note: proof is the measure of alcoholic strength in spirits
re is Latin-derived for 'about, regarding'
an ad, short for advertisement, is publicity

explanation.surface: A distiller's report on how strong a spirit is and how it was advertised, all checked for mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: To proofread is to read copy closely and correct any mistakes before printing.

clue.text: Much to take out, ignoring article stuck in individual block

indicators.note: one group of letters is pushed inside the word for individual

parts.note: a person is an individual

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the phrase much to take are jumbled
ignoring says the article's letter is left out of the jumble

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone told to remove a great deal finds a single person in the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal and 'ignoring article' drops the A from the fodder before it is shuffled; 'block' is a verb here, meaning thwart.
explanation.definitionFit: To put the mockers on a plan is a British idiom for spoiling or thwarting it, so to stop it happening.

clue.text: Single call to arms not entirely hard to deliver?

parts.note: single means one

indicators.note: not entirely says the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a rouse is a military signal calling soldiers to arms

explanation.surface: A lone rallying cry, only partly given, proves hard to get across.
explanation.definitionFit: Something burdensome is a heavy task, hard to carry out or fulfil, as an onerous duty is.

clue.text: Lethal error I overlooked — ingesting astatine

indicators.note: ingesting means swallowing, so one piece goes inside the other
overlooked says the letter I is ignored and dropped

parts.note: a fail is an error or failure
At is the chemical symbol for astatine

explanation.surface: A deadly mistake missed in a lab where a radioactive element has been swallowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethal and deadly are synonyms, describing something that causes death.

clue.text: Equestrian competition unfinished still

indicators.note: unfinished says the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: eventing, or an event, is a horse-riding contest

explanation.surface: A horse-riding contest is still not over.
explanation.definitionFit: Still and even both work as intensifiers: 'still better' and 'even better' mean the same.

clue.text: I overacted wildly to no real purpose?

indicators.note: wildly signals that the letters of i overacted are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: An actor admits hamming it up pointlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornamental things are there for show rather than use, which the question mark flags as a playful definition.

clue.text: Points to copy when taken on by chartered surveyor

indicators.note: taken on by means held within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: CS is an abbreviation for chartered surveyor
to ape is to copy or imitate

explanation.surface: A surveyor is engaged and promptly mimicked on several points.
explanation.definitionFit: Headlands jutting into the sea are points of land, as in Cape Horn.

clue.text: Case closed, tidied up, without a second being amalgamated

indicators.note: tidied up signals the letters of case closed are rearranged
without says that one letter is left out of the rearranged letters

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for a second

explanation.surface: A detective's file is shut and tidied, two parts merged in an instant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tidied up' rearranges CASE CLOSED, from which one S ('a second') is removed ('without').
explanation.definitionFit: Things that have merged into one whole have amalgamated; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Nationalist group (not large) kept in touch

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so the group's word goes inside the other

parts.note: to pat is to touch lightly
a trio is a small group of three

explanation.surface: A small political faction stays in contact.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who fervently supports their country can be called a nationalist or patriot.

clue.text: Indication of failing powers to support juvenile criminal

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it
a child is a juvenile
a hood, short for hoodlum, is a criminal

explanation.surface: A sign of weakening authority in backing a young offender.
explanation.walkthrough: SECOND comes first because a supporter is placed beneath what it supports in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Childish behaviour in old age is a sign of declining mental faculties.

clue.text: Tense pressure applied to soldiers in focus of operations

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
heat means pressure, as in 'the heat is on'
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Tension mounts as pressure is put on troops at the centre of a campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operations' looks military, but it means surgery: the operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgery takes place in an operating theatre, and a war's area of action is also its theatre.

clue.text: Confused conversation I caught about love

indicators.note: about says the pieces go around the letter for love

parts.note: a chat is a conversation
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
c is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A muddled chat in which someone was caught talking about romance.
explanation.definitionFit: A disordered, chaotic situation is a confused, jumbled one.

clue.text: Work during holiday leading to a disturbance

indicators.note: during says the work goes inside the holiday word

parts.note: hol is a British abbreviation for holiday
an op, or opus, is a piece of work

explanation.surface: Being made to work on holiday leads to a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuss or commotion, a bit of excitement and noise, is a hoopla.

clue.text: Describing water-source from China, say, probed by European broadcaster

indicators.note: probed by means entered by, so the broadcaster goes inside

parts.note: a Chinese person, or China itself, is an example of something Asian
RTE is Ireland's national broadcaster

explanation.surface: An Irish channel investigates the source of water in China.
explanation.definitionFit: An artesian well taps groundwater under pressure, so the adjective describes that kind of water supply.

clue.text: Crisis memo elaborated minor earthquake

indicators.note: elaborated means worked up, so the letters of crisis memo are reworked

explanation.surface: A detailed emergency memo about a small tremor.
explanation.definitionFit: A microseism is a faint earth tremor, too small to feel, as the prefix micro suggests.

clue.text: Unusually harsh cement used around Olympic venue

indicators.note: used around says one word is wrapped round the other

parts.note: mastic is a putty-like cement
Sochi, in Russia, hosted the 2014 Winter Olympics

explanation.surface: Severe building materials were laid around an Olympic stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' looks like an anagram signal but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who enjoys inflicting pain on themselves is strikingly severe towards themselves.

clue.text: No fighting now — start to consider calm following fury

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: ease is calm or relaxation
fire means fury or passion

explanation.surface: A plea to think calmly after rage and stop the fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A truce is a halt to hostilities, an agreement that no further shots are fired.

clue.text: Who'll do for criminal etc?

indicators.note: criminal signals that the letters of etc are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Asking who will catch the villain and his kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do for' means bring down; the whole clue describes a detective while 'criminal' also rearranges ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: A tec is a slang word for a detective, the person who brings offenders to justice.

clue.text: Odd elements in crude suggestion

indicators.note: the odd letters, first, third and fifth, of the word crude

explanation.surface: A rough hint made up of strange bits.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is a hint or prompt, a suggestion of what to do next.

clue.text: Revealed by stance adopted by editor

indicators.note: adopted by means taken in, so these pieces go inside the editor's letters

parts.note: x is the times sign, read as 'by' in measurements such as 3 x 4
a pose is a stance or posture

explanation.surface: A position taken up by an editor is laid bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid open to view or uncovered means the same as revealed.

clue.text: Turned up to get rice dished out — promise to turn up again?

parts.note: arrived means turned up

indicators.note: dished out signals that the letters of rice are served up in another order

explanation.surface: Someone arrives for a rice dish and says they'll be back.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian farewell means 'until we see each other again', implying a return.

clue.text: Former car company revived after article penned

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, so the article goes inside the other word

parts.note: a fire that is relit is revived
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A defunct car maker is brought back after a feature is written.
explanation.walkthrough: Reliant was a British maker of three-wheeled cars such as the Robin.
explanation.definitionFit: Reliant was a British vehicle manufacturer, now gone, best known for three-wheelers.

clue.text: Crowd in rear of cafe accordingly getting coffee

indicators.note: rear of means the last letter of the word cafe
in says the crowd's word is put inside the other letters

parts.note: so means accordingly or therefore
to press, or a press, is a crowd

explanation.surface: A crowd at the back of a cafe means people are getting their caffeine.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is strong black coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans.

clue.text: Apparently laid-up, as announced?

definitions.meaning: a cryptic sense: laid up means poorly and confined, and the word visibly holds a sickness word within a sleeping-place word
advertised or publicised in advance, as a show's star is

explanation.surface: Someone seemingly stuck in bed, as was declared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apparently' flags a visual reading: ILL sits inside B-ED, so the word looks like someone poorly in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer advertised to appear has been publicised in advance, so promoted ahead of the show.

clue.text: Bar contributing to closing others

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pub plays its part in shutting down rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a block of cast metal, such as a gold bar.

clue.text: Declines to overlook official applications

indicators.note: to overlook means to leave out, so the official's letters are dropped

parts.note: refuses means declines
a ref, or referee, is a sports official

explanation.surface: Turning down requests so as to bypass a bureaucrat.
explanation.definitionFit: The applications of a tool are the purposes or functions it is put to.

clue.text: Fish dish? I miss a fish's tail in a stew

indicators.note: in a stew means in a muddle, so the letters are mixed up
tail means the last letter of the word fish's, taken without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A diner worried about missing the end of a fish stew.
explanation.walkthrough: The tail of FISH is H; with the apostrophe s ignored, 'in a stew' mixes it with I MISS A.
explanation.definitionFit: Sashimi is a Japanese dish of thinly sliced raw fish.

clue.text: Cactus very much requiring intervention of a protector? Not entirely

indicators.note: intervention means coming between, so these letters go inside the other word

parts.note: so means very much, as in 'so happy'

indicators.note: not entirely says the last letter is removed

parts.note: a guard is a protector

explanation.surface: A prickly plant that badly needs a guardian, at least in part.
explanation.definitionFit: The saguaro is the giant tree-like cactus of the Arizona desert.

clue.text: New fiddle not seeing debut in gentle movement

indicators.note: debut means the first letter, which is not seen, so it is dropped

parts.note: to fudge is to fiddle or fake figures

explanation.surface: A new violin, not yet launched, moves gently.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudge is a slight push, such as a gentle prod with the elbow.

clue.text: Incorrectly reported: it should be "Overlooked collecting rubbish"

indicators.note: collecting means taking in, so the rubbish goes inside the other word

parts.note: missed means overlooked
tat is British slang for cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: A correction notice: a report on gathering rubbish was wrongly worded.
explanation.definitionFit: Something misstated has been described wrongly or inaccurately.
